note: The renderer registry. render_common.py reads `tools` to probe this machine and to compare what it found against the pinned build in cua-applications.csv; render_files.py reads `formats[kind]` to turn a file into page images. Supporting a new file type is an entry here, not a code change.
parity_note: `parity_app` names the row in cua-applications.csv that this tool stands in for on the CUA Ubuntu VM. Only the tools that decide LAYOUT carry one — an office suite, a browser, a 3D renderer. A rasteriser like pdftoppm turns an already-laid-out PDF into pixels and has no VM counterpart, so it needs no parity target.
requires_note: A format renders faithfully when every tool in `requires` is present AND, where `one_of` is given, at least one of those is. `one_of` holds interchangeable tools — any PDF rasteriser will do. The degraded fallbacks in render_files.py (a Quick Look thumbnail) never satisfy a requirement; they exist so a missing renderer still shows page 1 while being reported as not visually verifiable.

pymupdf.unlocks: PDF -> page images + text (no system package needed)

acquire.note: A wheel in the workspace venv, so PDFs render on a host with no system packages at all. Unversioned on purpose: it rasterises a layout that is already fixed in the file, so it has no VM counterpart to match.

soffice.parity_note: LibreOffice is the parity renderer: every CUA task is Ubuntu-only, so the VM's office suite is LibreOffice, not MS Office. A different build repaginates, and pagination is what the visual criteria grade.

hint.darwin: python3 provision_renderers.py soffice --install   (pinned build; `brew install --cask libreoffice` gives the latest instead)
hint.linux: python3 provision_renderers.py soffice --install   (pinned build; `apt-get install -y libreoffice` gives the distro's instead)

acquire.note: The Document Foundation keeps every past release, so the CSV's pinned version is installable as-is rather than approximated by 'latest'.

wrapper.note: A private user profile: headless conversion must not touch, or be blocked by, the operator's own LibreOffice session.

fonts-parity.unlocks: LibreOffice substitutes nothing: the same metrics as the CUA Ubuntu VM
fonts-parity.parity_note: Fonts are part of parity. Carlito carries Calibri's metrics and Caladea carries Cambria's; without them a DOCX written in Calibri reflows, so the line breaks and page counts you would then 'verify' are not the contributor's.

hint.darwin: python3 provision_renderers.py soffice --install   (all four families ship inside LibreOffice)
hint.linux: apt-get install -y fonts-crosextra-carlito fonts-crosextra-caladea fonts-liberation fonts-liberation2 fonts-dejavu-core

office.note: Converted to PDF by LibreOffice, then rasterised. Both halves must work; the rasteriser is interchangeable and has no parity requirement, the converter is neither.

html.note: HTML has real layout, unlike plain text. Chrome headless screenshots it; without Chrome its appearance is UNVERIFIABLE, not 'no layout'.

render.skip_note: audio has no visual layout; its content is UNVERIFIABLE from frames
render.note: One frame every 10s, capped by the page budget. Anything between samples is unseen.

media.note: Without ffmpeg a video's visual asks are UNVERIFIABLE; metadata only.

render.note: Frame 1 of the scene's active camera, forced to Cycles on CPU. A .blend with no camera renders nothing, which is a failed render, not a defect.

blender.note: Without blender a .blend is UNVERIFIABLE; metadata only.

postscript.note: Ghostscript converts to PDF, then the PDF renderer rasterises it.

render.note: First layer/page only — a multi-layer composite is not judged here.

raster_exotic.note: Raster formats the Read tool cannot display, so handing over the original would claim a verifiable appearance nobody can see.

render.note: Every frame, not just the first: a TIFF is most often a multi-page scan, and page 1 is not the file.
